title: Power Apps: modern, refreshed look reaches embedded model-driven apps on the semiannual channel
summary: The roadmap facts, default state, licensing context and environment release-channel controls are supported. Two minor corrections remain: cite Microsoft's statement that the modern look does not affect data or permissions, and remove the checklist instruction to check app and user overrides because those controls have no table rows.

claims.claim: The semi-annual channel turns on GA-ready features in April and October.
claims.quote: The semi-annual channel turns on generally available (GA) ready features twice a year, in April and October.

claims.claim: Semi-annual releases follow a gradual weekly rollout.
claims.quote: Like the monthly channel, each semi-annual release follows the gradual weekly rollout across the same region groups, starting with the first release region and reaching each subsequent region group on the following weekend.

claims.claim: An environment receives a feature's build on its regional rollout schedule rather than one date shared by all environments.
claims.quote: Because builds roll out to the region groups over successive weekends, the date an environment receives a given build depends on its region group.

claims.claim: Channel checks are ordered URL override, user override, non-Auto app channel, then non-Auto environment channel.
claims.quote:
1. URL override.
2. User channel override.
3. App release channel value other than Auto (for example, Monthly, Semi-annual).
4. Environment release channel value other than Auto (for example, Monthly, Semi-annual).

claims.claim: The environment channel is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Behavior > Release channel > Model-driven app release channel.
claims.quote:
select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Behavior.

| Model-driven app release channel |

claims.claim: The environment release channel can govern when model-driven app features arrive, subject to the documented app and user qualifications.
claims.quote: The environment channel can be set using the Power Platform admin center or with code. ... Developers can change the environment channel by updating the ReleaseChannel column value for the row in the Organization table.

claims.claim: The release channel is a general feature-availability control rather than a setting specific to this visual refresh.
claims.quote: You can control how often the users in your organization get these new features by specifying the release channel. ... The release channel controls feature availability.

claims.claim: The channel-change page says Power Platform model-driven apps use Monthly when the app channel is Auto regardless of the environment channel.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps in Power Platform environments use Monthly when the app release channel is Auto regardless of the environment release channel. All model-driven apps in Power Platform environments need to set the app release channel explicitly.

claims.claim: Makers can set an app's channel through the app designer or the Solutions area.
claims.quote: Use the app channel to override the release channel for a model-driven app by using Power Apps app designer or the Solutions area.

claims.claim: The modern-look page says admins can turn off New Look using the New look for model driven apps setting.
claims.quote: Admins can turn off the New Look for all users by updating the New look for model driven apps app setting.

claims.claim: The app-properties page says the New Look setting is hidden and ignored once the new look becomes mandatory.
claims.quote: This setting is hidden and ignored with the 2026 Wave 1 release when the new look becomes mandatory.

claims.claim: Neither the modern-look page nor the app-properties page states whether the legacy New Look switch covers embedded app experiences.
claims.quote: Searched: "New look for model driven apps" "embedded" setting; opened modern-fluent-design and app-properties. Neither ties the legacy switch to embedded hosts; the latter says it is hidden and ignored.
